new_realizations.coverage_method: Scope: the 56 keys with previous_review_exists=false in realization-review-v3/manifest.json (54 approved and 2 not approved, 56 in total). The 87 old keys were not re-reviewed, as instructed. Payloads: I read every one of the 56 v3 new_payload objects in review-deltas.json in full: units, fragments, scan and page labels, conditions, condition instructions, wording_selection, variants and readings, source_fidelity and attesting_controls with their settings and hashes, quotations, source_reference_part, corrections, source_notes and speakers. I did not reuse earlier approvals by inferring a diff. Every approval here rests on a fresh full read of the current v3 content. I spot-checked one per-key file (realization__musaf_al_yevoshu__he.json) and it matched its new_payload by inspection. I had no hashing tool, so I did not check payload-file SHA-256 against the manifest. Code and guidelines: build.py lines 1-720 (quotation_words, rubric_words, unit_document, segment/reference/condition/canonical/join_next/end_reference handling) and JLPTEI-3.md lines 1-600 (URN scope, terminators, quote-context, versification, sub-verse scope). I did not read readings.json or the rest of corrections.json; the data approval rests on the payloads and generated XML. compile-qa-v3: verse-projections.json lines 1-150. I did not open compiler-report.json, assertions.json or source-projections.json, so the 52-profile and 19-occurrence claims are taken as reported, not independently verified here. Specific checks: Isaiah 44:6 EN whole verse is inside its milestone and seg, with 'And it was said:' outside. Malkhuyot close HE yields 'הַשַּׁבָּת וְ<endConditional/>יִשְׂרָאֵל', with no detached prefix. The Ansikhah EN source note has language=en and spacing is fixed. The Frankfurt abbreviations are copied as printed (פפ״דמ quiet, פפד״מ repetition), each with abbr/expan. Heye quote contexts use .../N/quotes/book_c_v/book_c/v throughout. The veneemar condition is used only in the spine (al_yevoshu_custom, together with rite frankfurt/metz=false); al_yevoshu.xml prints וְנֶאֱמַר unconditionally inside stanza 12. Jerusalem: the scan 254 Umippenei has printed yod 'וְלִירוּשָׁלַֽיִם' with no CGJ. The scan 266 Isaiah 24:23 in Ahallelah has 'וּבִירוּשָׁלַֽ͏ִם' (patah, meteg, CGJ, hiriq). Psalm 24:9: sic/corr covers the single word שְׂעוּ/שְׂאוּ in Ahallelah only (scan 268); Malkhuyot verses (scan 272) prints שְׂאוּ uncorrected. In rh_qedushat_hayom the first Attah prayer-part has an explicit terminator before the Vattitten milestone.

findings.location: prayerbook_for_the_new_year-heidenheim-1965-he/musaf_repetition_vattitten_lanu.xml (div corresp=urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/vattitten_lanu_hashem), its EN counterpart, and spine index.xml line 3352; compared with rh_qedushat_hayom.xml line 39
findings.problem: One printed text has two identities in the same project. The repetition Vattitten becomes a new canonical home for the generic URN prayer:amidah/vattitten_lanu_hashem. But the HE project already marks the same Rosh Hashanah Vattitten (same words; only meteg and maqaf differ, plus 'הַזֶּה.' and 'מִצְרָֽיִם') in rh_qedushat_hayom with prayer-part corresp=urn:x-opensiddur:text:siddur:rosh_hashanah/text/vattitten_lanu. This splits one text across two URNs. JLPTEI's quote-context rule says not to duplicate a canonical URN merely because the text is printed again, and the batch elsewhere reuses identity for reprinted texts (Attah vechartanu transcludes attah_vechartanu_mikol; Al ken and the offering formula use printing variants). vattitten_lanu_hashem is not among the 208 registry decisions, so it is a pre-existing master URN. Its existing master meaning (generic festival wording or the Rosh Hashanah wording) is not documented in this batch. I approved this key earlier without having opened rh_qedushat_hayom; that approval is withdrawn.
findings.required_change: Before installing, either (a) have the repetition transclude urn:x-opensiddur:text:siddur:rosh_hashanah/text/vattitten_lanu, recording the repetition-printing differences as wording variants as was done for Al ken and the offering formula, and update the spine transclusion; or (b) document in the registry evidence that prayer:amidah/vattitten_lanu_hashem already denotes this Rosh Hashanah wording in the corpus, and resolve the duplicate project-level identity by retiring one URN or recording an alias or relationship. Check the EN project in the same way, then regenerate and re-run reference validation and compile QA.

findings.problem: Same pattern as Vattitten: a pre-existing generic prayer URN (not among this batch's registry decisions) becomes the canonical home for the Rosh Hashanah Umippenei wording ('...וְאֶת מוּסְפֵי יוֹם (הַשַּׁבָּת הַזֶּה וְיוֹם) הַזִּכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה...', with the Avinu Malkenu clause). Unlike Vattitten, I found no competing identity for this text in the project, so the key stays approved, but the master meaning of the URN is undocumented.
findings.required_change: Confirm in the registry evidence that umipenay_chataaynu_galinu is meant to cover the Rosh Hashanah Musaf wording, or not a different festival wording. If it is not, use a Rosh Hashanah-specific identity before installing.

findings.problem: A Codex-authored HE description note 'תקיעה, שברים, תרועה, תקיעה.' sits right before a transclusion of the literal printed shofar_calls text 'תקיעה: שברים: תרועה: תקיעה:'. The Hebrew output therefore shows the calls twice. The EN gloss is useful because there is no source English, but the HE note only repeats the printed words.
findings.required_change: Drop the Codex HE description note, keeping the blower role note and the EN gloss, or confirm in visual QA that the duplication is intended.

findings.location: HE musaf_heyeh_im_pifiyot.xml stanza 11 (milestone unit=chapter n=33 and unit=verse n=19 without corresp); EN musaf_numbers_28_words.xml (milestone unit=chapter n=28 without corresp)
findings.problem: Under JLPTEI rule 3, a milestone with a unit but no corresp is a terminator: these markers open nothing and only display numbers. The versification table also says unit=verse requires a canonical corresp. Scopes resolve correctly: the half-verse 33:19/b and verses 28:9-10 are bounded and no whole verse or chapter is claimed. This is the pattern accepted by the order review and by my earlier recommendation, but the guideline does not describe it.
findings.required_change: Non-blocking. Record the convention that a numbered milestone without corresp is a context-only terminator in the project encoding notes, or ask for a guideline sentence.
